body: Friday, August 28 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: Fed Chair Warsh delivered a hawkish Jackson Hole speech today, explicitly flagging inflation concerns and stating "we have work to do." Rate-hike expectations are rising. The 2Y yield at 4.20% (prior close, −3 bps vs 4W) is little changed, while the 10Y at 4.72% is marginally lower (−2 bps vs 4W), leaving the curve at +47 bps — positively sloped but still flat by historical standards. VIX at 14.47 reflects complacency despite the hawkish pivot. Fiscal stance remains expansionary with the Trump administration eyeing Venezuelan oil stakes amid diesel at reported elevated levels.

New / Most Important: Warsh's Jackson Hole debut was the week's defining event. He broke with market expectations of a dovish lean, openly discussing further rate hikes to contain inflation. A mysterious $912 million position was moved before the speech, suggesting leakage or anticipatory positioning by a well-connected player. Markets held steady on the surface — S&P 500 at 7705 (+2.9% vs 4W), Nasdaq 100 at 29405 (+4.0%) — but bond markets zigzagged intraday. This is structurally important: Warsh is a new Fed Chair who is establishing his credibility playbook. Unlike Powell's gradualist communication style, Warsh appears willing to front-run hawkish action with blunt rhetoric, which creates a new regime for how markets must discount Fed communication. The era of forward guidance as soothing balm is over; Warsh is treating Jackson Hole as a tool to tighten financial conditions through jawboning before actually moving rates. Watch whether the "mysterious trader" story gains traction — if front-running is confirmed, it would be a serious institutional credibility issue for the Fed.

Playbook ✓: AI mega-cap leadership continues to dominate — Nasdaq outperforming Russell by 2.2% over 4 weeks, classic narrow market. Microsoft breaking out, Amazon jumping on earnings/positioning. BofA doubling down on Nvidia. The AI rally narrative per NYT is "just getting started."  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Gold surging +11.9% to $4529 while Bitcoin rips +19.9% to $77,819 is deeply unusual alongside a hawkish Fed pivot. In a normal playbook, a hawkish Fed = stronger dollar = gold/crypto weakness. Instead, both hard assets are screaming higher. Soft growth gauges tell you this isn't a risk-on move — a Reuters poll sees China's factory activity contracting again in August and US new home sales fell 10.5% in July — it's a parallel debasement/fear trade running alongside equity euphoria. This divergence suggests the market is pricing two contradictory regimes simultaneously: (1) Warsh hikes and maintains USD credibility, and (2) fiscal dominance makes real rates negative regardless. The $912M mystery trade may be the tell — someone large is betting the hawkish talk won't translate to sustained real tightening.

Macro Stance: The ECB is in an active tightening posture. July meeting accounts revealed hawks were ready to hike at that meeting, and inflation is set to rise further. A September rate hike is now widely expected. Lending dynamics are mixed — bank lending to businesses fell again in July, but broader lending growth picked up. The euro is gaining on the hawkish policy outlook.

New / Most Important: The ECB accounts published this week confirmed a deeply hawkish internal tilt, with hawks citing a "credit surge" as justification for further tightening. Eurozone inflation is set to rise, per Morningstar, reinforcing the September hike case. This is a significant divergence from the growth picture — Czech GDP grew only 0.4% in Q2, and business lending is contracting even as the ECB prepares to tighten further. The ECB is walking into a policy error setup where they hike into weakening credit demand.

Playbook ✓: Euro strengthening on hawkish ECB relative to expectations — classic rate differential trade. Policy divergence between ECB (hiking) and some EM central banks (holding/cutting) is widening carry spreads predictably.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The contradiction between falling business lending and the ECB citing a "credit surge" as justification for hikes suggests the ECB is looking at household credit while ignoring corporate credit contraction. This is a classic late-cycle policy error pattern. If the ECB hikes in September while business lending continues to contract, the euro's strength will be self-defeating for exporters, and we could see an acceleration in European industrial weakness by Q4. The market is not pricing this tail risk — euro longs are consensus and crowded.

Macro Stance: The easing bias runs through liquidity and a managed currency, not rates. The PBOC held the LPRs for a 15th month while expanding consumer and small-business loan subsidies (The Asian Banker, [Aug 21]), ran a 500 billion yuan MLF operation (BigGo Finance, [Aug 24]) and keeps conducting overnight reverse repos (Fibre2Fashion, [Aug 26]). The yuan is the pressure point: it reached a three-year high against the dollar (UA.NEWS, [Aug 27]) and edged higher in a tight range ahead of Jackson Hole (Business Recorder, [Aug 27]), with the PBOC cautious on gains despite dollar weakness (SCMP, [Aug 27]) after a weaker fix signalled tolerance for depreciation (VT Markets, [Aug 25]): the PBOC is applying the brakes, not reversing the yuan (Exchange Rates UK, [Aug 27]). July CPI slowed to 0.5% and PPI to 3.5%, both missing expectations (BigGo Finance, [Aug 8]).

PMIs & Activity: The pulse stays below 50 into the August PMIs. July's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.2 and non-manufacturing to 49.0 (FXStreet, [Jul 31]), the private factory index eased to 50.9 (Fibre2Fashion, [Aug 3]), and a Reuters poll sees factory activity contracting again in August (Reuters, [Aug 27]). July industrial output grew 4.5% y/y and retail sales only 0.6% (Reuters, [Aug 17]); exports jumped almost a quarter (Financial Times, [Aug 6]). Industrial profits rose 17.6% in January-July (Xinhua, [Aug 27]), growth hitting a seven-month low as the AI boom fails to mask weak demand (BigGo Finance, [Aug 27]), while semiconductor profits soared 18.5-fold (Global Times, [Aug 27]). Domestic demand is weakest in autos, where sales slumped 22% even as NEV penetration hit 64.3% (GlobalChinaEV, [Aug 27]).

Credit Impulse: July bank loans posted a record contraction as credit demand faltered (Reuters, [Aug 14]), yet credit growth exceeded forecasts despite the rare loan slump (Bloomberg, [Aug 14]). Reconciled: the broad financing aggregate is holding up while the loan book shrank, so the impulse comes from outside bank lending. Policy is targeting rather than expanding credit: the subsidized loan program was expanded to revive demand (Caixin Global, [Aug 21]) and banks are launching "token loans" to fund AI firms (Caixin Global, [Aug 26]), while online lender FinVolution reports China funding tightening (Investing.com, [Aug 27]).

Property: July new home prices were stagnant as demand stayed weak (Reuters, [Aug 17]); the 70-city annual decline narrowed to 3.2% while property investment slumped nearly 20% (BigGo Finance, [Aug 17]). A Reuters poll sees home prices falling slightly less this year but the investment slump deepening (Reuters, [Aug 27]), which reconciles China Daily's signs of rebound (China Daily Global Edition, [Aug 27]) with the developer data. Vanke posted a $2.2 billion loss as debt pressure mounts (Bloomberg, [Aug 27]), an H1 net loss of RMB 14.95B with revenue down 33% and a net debt ratio of 135.4% (TradingView, [Aug 27]), and its losses widen even as cities roll out new property measures (Nikkei Asia, [Aug 27]). Provident fund rules are being reshaped (China.org.cn, [Aug 21]) and liquidators can pursue PwC globally over Evergrande (Financial Times, [Aug 26]).

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: The vice-premier calls for proactive fiscal policy (China Daily, [Aug 27]) and signals fiscal reform to ease pressure on local governments (SCMP, [Aug 27]); S&P affirmed China's A+ rating and sees growth above 4% as fiscal support continues (TradingView, [Aug 27]). The Economist argues China should be loosening budgetary policy but is doing the opposite (The Economist, [Aug 27]), with 7.7 bln yuan of overdue tax demanded from over 100 listed firms (The Standard, [Aug 26]) and the $119 billion financing tool facing a roll-out lag (Reuters, [Aug 24]). On trade, China opposes the US plan for 7.5% tariffs and warns of countermeasures (Yeni Şafak English, [Aug 27]) as it weighs a response (Bloomberg, [Aug 27]), while its foreign minister calls on both sides to overcome obstacles before the summit (The Washington Post, [Aug 27]); a Dutch think-tank pushes the EU for tougher tariffs (EUobserver, [Aug 27]).

Markets & Flows: Mainland stocks ride the AI tape while Hong Kong lags: China stocks climbed on the Nvidia-led AI hardware rally (TradingView, [Aug 26]), but the Hang Seng fell to 25,565.74 as Nvidia euphoria faded (BBN Times, [Aug 27]) after a US power grid ban jolted Hong Kong stocks (BigGo Finance, [Aug 27]). Morgan Stanley pivots to A-shares and sees Hong Kong regaining momentum later in September (BigGo Finance, [Aug 27]).

New / Most Important: Vanke's results and the August PMI poll point the same way. Vanke lost RMB 14.95B in the half with net gearing at 135.4%, even as cities add property measures, and economists expect the factory PMI to stay in contraction. The credit and property legs of the growth pulse are still weakening, so the next easing step depends on fiscal policy that The Economist says is tightening.

Playbook ✓: Targeted easing, a managed yuan, developer stress and AI-led mainland equities are on script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: A three-year high in the yuan alongside a sub-50 PMI and a deepening property investment slump is not a recovery signal; it is the dollar's weakness meeting a demand-starved economy. Transmission runs through property and steel: with Vanke stressed and the investment slump deepening, iron ore rose on stimulus signals (TradingView, [Aug 24]) only after weakening despite them (TradingView, [Aug 23]), leaving the AUD exposed; European exporters face weak Chinese demand and a tougher EU line, and WTI at $83.51 is a terms-of-trade tax on Chinese margins.

Macro Stance: The BOJ is on the verge of accelerating its tightening campaign. Multiple sources confirmed this week that the BOJ is expected to raise its key rate to 1.25% in September. Tokyo inflation data rose, reinforcing the case. Deputy Governor Himino drove home inflation risks while stopping short of an explicit hint, maintaining optionality.

New / Most Important: This is structurally the most important development in global macro this week alongside Warsh. The BOJ is now set to "speed up" its tightening campaign — not just normalize, but accelerate. Reuters reported a move to 1.25% in September, which would represent a pace of hiking that the market had not anticipated as recently as a month ago. The Takaichi political dimension adds complexity — yen weakness is creating political pressure that actually reinforces the BOJ's hawkish hand rather than constraining it. Commerzbank stated explicitly that "anything else would likely put the Japanese Yen under significant pressure," meaning the BOJ is now boxed into hiking to defend the currency. This creates a reflexive loop: yen weakness → political pressure → BOJ hike → carry trade unwind → potential global volatility. The G20 attendance by Japan's finance minister and BOJ chief signals they want to coordinate messaging on the yen. Watch JPY crosses closely — if the September hike materializes, the second-order effect on global carry trades (particularly AUD/JPY, MXN/JPY) could be violent.

Playbook ✓: BOJ normalization continues to follow the script of gradual but accelerating tightening. Tokyo inflation data supporting the move is textbook.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The acceleration from "gradual" to "speed up" is the divergence itself. The consensus was for slow, well-telegraphed moves. Speed changes the game for carry traders globally.

Macro Stance: The RBA is in a hawkish hold with rising probability of another hike. The August meeting minutes revealed the board debated a rate hike, with the board divided. July inflation ran hot, and three of four major Australian banks now forecast another hike this year. AUD is gaining on hawkish RBA outlook.

New / Most Important: Australia's July inflation print came in higher than expected, triggering a market repricing of rate hike risk. The RBA's internal division — debating a hike — is new information that shifts probabilities. The Guardian flagged "fears of a fourth rate hike," which means the cumulative tightening burden on Australian households (heavily mortgage-exposed) is becoming a macro risk in itself. This is a classic Antipodean doom loop: hot inflation → forced hike → mortgage stress → consumption drag → but services inflation stays sticky because of immigration-driven demand.

Playbook ✓: AUD strength on rate differentials is textbook.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: If the BOJ accelerates hikes simultaneously, AUD/JPY carry unwind could overwhelm any RBA hawkishness benefit to AUD. The cross-asset correlation risk is underpriced.

Macro Stance: The NBP is on hold at 3.75% with inflation pressure described as moderate (CEO Magazyn, [Aug 28]), but the debate inside the RPP has shifted: the minutes revealed which members wanted a hike (Tysol.pl, [Aug 22]), the Council expects inflation to persist and worries about global market turbulence (Business Insider Polska, [Aug 27]), and the question now asked is whether the next move could be up (Tysol.pl, [Aug 26]). The two-sided squeeze remains: ABN AMRO's divergence against a hawkish ECB and BNY's import pass-through risk. Activity holds up: July retail sales rose 3.9% y/y in constant prices (Inwestycje.pl, [Aug 24]), slightly below expectations (Miesięcznik Finansowy BANK, [Aug 24]); industry was strong while construction surprised with a decline (CEO Magazyn, [Aug 26]); investment has become the engine of Q2 growth (Bankier.pl, [Aug 28]). The GUS average wage crossed 9500 zł (Direct Money, [Aug 21]). The caveat is the horizon: the finance ministry itself warned of a slowdown (Bankier.pl, [Aug 28]).

Markets: A nasty week. Thursday brought the biggest sell-off in over two months (Bankier.pl, [Aug 27]) with the WIG20 the weakest index in Europe (Business Insider Polska, [Aug 27]); Parkiet tied the outflow from GPW and the zloty to the CIA chief's visit and an aversion to Polish assets [Aug 27], Kruk fell 7% and CD Projekt traded on huge turnover (CrypS.pl, [Aug 27]). Friday was a draw (Parkiet, [Aug 28]): Allegro led while Modivo and Kruk closed lower (Inwestycje.pl, [Aug 28]) and Orlen recovered to be the WIG20's main support (DNA Rynków, [Aug 28]). Before the shock the index had been welded to 4000 points (Parkiet, [Aug 25]) and PKO BP printed an all-time high (DNA Rynków, [Aug 26]). The card shows damage concentrated in gaming and energy: CD Projekt -8.4% on the week, Orlen -5.3%, Pekao -2.2%, EPOL at 43.58 (-1.3% 1W, +1.9% 4W); the winners were KGHM at 361.6 (+8.8% 1W, +16.9% 4W), Dino at 35.44 (+9.8% 1W, +11.3% 4W) and PGE (+5.4% 1W). The zloty reversed: after USD/PLN hit a two-month low (Comparic.pl, [Aug 22]) near 3.68 (CEO Magazyn, [Aug 21]), the euro became the dearest in over a month (Bankier.pl, [Aug 28]) with EUR/PLN near 4.34 and USD/PLN heading for 3.75 ahead of the Fed chair's Jackson Hole speech (CEO Magazyn, [Aug 28]). The card has USD/PLN at 3.7164 (+0.7% 1W, -0.5% 4W) and EUR/PLN at 4.3303 (+0.4% 1W, +0.6% 4W). POLGBs are the sore point: 10-year yields reached levels not seen since May (Interia Biznes, [Aug 28]), and CEO Magazyn argued the new peaks are not about the budget [Aug 28].

Fiscal & Politics: The government adopted the 2027 draft budget today: a state deficit of 282.6 bn zł, a general government deficit of 7.1% of GDP, growth of 3.6% this year and 3% next (Gazeta Prawna, [Aug 28]; Reuters, [Aug 28]). ING called it not great, not terrible and the sixth consecutive year of excessive deficit [Aug 28]; Business Insider Polska quoted the line that the government is testing markets' patience [Aug 28]; Domański conceded a significant rise in debt-servicing costs (Interia Biznes, [Aug 28]). The mix is electoral: health up 26 bn zł (PAP, [Aug 28]), less on defence (Gazeta Prawna, [Aug 28]), the alcohol excise hike returning and new PIT thresholds (Money.pl and Gazeta Prawna, [Aug 28]), after earlier reporting of a rate rising from 19 to 22% from 2027 (Gazeta Prawna, [Aug 21]). Fitch affirmed the rating but warned on deficit and record debt (CEO Magazyn, [Aug 22]), and SocGen said budget risks point to further zloty weakness versus the euro [Aug 24]. President Nawrocki vetoed three of seven bills (Gazeta Prawna, [Aug 28]) and energy-sector taxes hinge on his signature (Business Insider Polska, [Aug 28]). Almost 100% of EU recovery funds are allocated (TVP World, [Aug 28]).

Corporate & Sectors: Banks mix records and risks: July mortgage lending hit a record 14.8 bn zł (Bankier.pl, [Aug 24]), over a fifth of it refinancing [Aug 27]; the sector posted a historic profit and 2.1 trillion in deposits (Bankier.pl, [Aug 28]), yet CIT held half-year earnings to only 21.4 bn zł [Aug 27], KNF warned free-credit sanction risk is rising fast (Business Insider Polska, [Aug 28]), PKO BP is contesting a 47.5 mln zł fine (pb.pl, [Aug 26]) and KNF recognised POLSTR as a significant benchmark (Gazeta Prawna, [Aug 25]). KGHM is the winner: world's largest silver producer with 712 tonnes in a half year (Next Gazeta.pl, [Aug 28]), copper resources up 61% (Parkiet, [Aug 26]), room to lift the dividend (Strefa Inwestorów, [Aug 25]), though unions want 6500 zł per employee [Aug 27]. Orlen's Baltic Power is 89% complete (WysokieNapiecie.pl, [Aug 28]); Tauron estimated 586 mln zł Q2 net profit (Inwestycje.pl, [Aug 25]). CD Projekt announced a Witcher 3 remaster (Bankier.pl, [Aug 26]) but Parkiet says the fourth Witcher will take longer [Aug 26] and investors kept selling (FXMAG, [Aug 27]); half-year results come next Wednesday. Dino has a fresh buy rating (pb.pl, [Aug 25]) and is up 34% since July (Comparic.pl, [Aug 25]); Couche-Tard launched a formal tender for all of Żabka (Reuters, [Aug 26]). Diesel returns above 8 zł from September as the CPN repeat ends (Next Gazeta.pl, [Aug 28]).

Geopolitics & Security: The CIA chief's reported warning to the Kremlin not to attack NATO (The Guardian, [Aug 27]) is what rattled Warsaw. Sikorski urged faster defence preparation (Українська правда, [Aug 28]); Polish F-16s suffered a system failure during a Russian missile breach (The New Voice of Ukraine, [Aug 28]); Poland signed a $2.2B Piorun missile deal (Anadolu, [Aug 24]); US Patriot stocks in Europe are beyond critical because of the Iran war (PBS, [Aug 27]).

New / Most Important: The 2027 budget is the story: a 7.1% deficit for a sixth year, financed into a market where 10-year yields are already at their highest since May and foreign money is leaving on security risk. Fitch's warning and SocGen's zloty call now have a number to anchor to.  |  Playbook ✓: PLN weakness on policy divergence is consensus; stay underweight duration, keep KGHM and Dino as earnings-backed longs.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The bond market blames geopolitics, not the budget, for the yield spike; if so, a de-escalation reprices POLGBs faster than any fiscal fix would.

Macro Stance: Czech GDP grew 0.4% in Q2, driven by consumer spending. This tepid growth in a CEE economy typically more cyclically sensitive underscores the broader European slowdown. Nothing actionable for now, but it's a useful leading indicator for Eurozone demand.
New / Most Important: The 0.4% Q2 print is new data.  |  Playbook ✓: Consumer-led growth while industry lags is the European script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: None today.

Narrative: AI mega-cap leadership keeps powering the Nasdaq 100 (+4.0% vs 4W), and the week's prints reignited the trade, with enterprise software rallying alongside chips after Nvidia and Salesforce.

Reported: Salesforce rocketed 22% for its second-best day ever, leading a software rally (CNBC, [Aug 27]). Okta surged 20% pre-market as it beat and raised full-year guidance for the second time this year (TradingKey, [Aug 27]). Workday exceeded Q2 expectations, but the stock dropped (StockStory, [Aug 27]).

EPS Upside Watch: Nutanix — analysts increased their forecasts after better-than-expected Q4 results (Benzinga, [Aug 27]). Guidewire — reports next week, and Wall Street expects earnings growth (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 27]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The NYT's 'A.I. Debt Binge Endangering the Economy' is the counter-narrative, and Broadcom's $70B debt deal is Exhibit A, while Nvidia revealed the stunning cost of its circular finance binge (AFR, [Aug 27]). Levering up with the 10Y at 4.72% creates a maturity mismatch: AI revenue is uncertain and deferred, debt service is immediate, and the VIX at 14.47 prices none of it.

Narrative: Alphabet proving AI can strengthen its Search business is the consensus: AI as moat reinforcement rather than disruption for incumbent platforms, a re-rating from 'AI-disrupted' to 'AI-enhanced'.

Reported: Zoom beat quarterly forecasts and raised its full-year outlook, but its shares fell (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 26]) as soft Q3 profit guidance overshadowed the double beat (24/7 Wall St., [Aug 26]). Subscriber gains at Stan and publishing offset Nine's TV ad headwinds (AFR, [Aug 26]). JOYY's Q2 revenue rose 16% as AI drove growth, and it raised its full-year profit guidance (BigGo Finance, [Aug 25]).
EPS Upside Watch: None flagged.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Zoom falling on a beat and a raise shows the bar for platforms without a visible AI revenue line: the market re-rates incumbents only where AI shows up in the numbers, as at JOYY, and gives no credit for an expanded product line alone.

Narrative: A hawkish Warsh is constructive for bank NIMs if the +47 bps curve stays positively sloped, and JPMorgan poaching BofA's David Fishman for tech M&A shows banks positioning for AI deal flow, a capital-markets tailwind Canada's banks just confirmed.

Reported: RBC, TD and CIBC topped bank profit estimates (Reuters, [Aug 27]), with TD posting the biggest beat of the Big Six as wholesale banking profit soared (Financial Post, [Aug 27]). CIBC slid after earnings as a sale charge and a capital-ratio dip offset its profit beat (Quiver Quantitative, [Aug 27]).

EPS Upside Watch: TD — unlocked $141 million in AI value months ahead of schedule (PYMNTS.com, [Aug 27]), a cost lever on top of the capital-markets beat. BMO — plans to buy back shares after a strong quarter (WSJ, [Aug 25]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The SEC's proposed rules allowing companies to tell investors less (NYT) are a structural negative for financial transparency: they could erode the information edge that active managers and analysts rely on, an under-discussed cost to capital allocation.

Narrative: WTI at $83.51 (-1.4% vs 4W) is drifting lower despite geopolitical noise as the US rig count rose to its highest since April 2025, and the administration eyeing Venezuelan oil stakes adds political complexity.

Reported: CNOOC made a record interim profit on higher oil prices and output (Reuters, [Aug 26]). Woodside posted a 7% first-half profit rise while scrapping its clean energy target (Reuters, [Aug 24]). Sinopec's H1 profit rose 19.3% as its chemicals segment returned to profit after 16 quarters (BigGo Finance, [Aug 23]).
EPS Upside Watch: None flagged.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Rising rig counts alongside falling crude say supply discipline is breaking down. Demand explains the confusion: China's July factory PMI sat at 49.2 and a Reuters poll sees it contracting again in August, while the US and euro-zone flash PMIs accelerated, so the answer is probably both, more US supply and tepid demand outside AI electricity.

Narrative: Copper strength (+3.5%) on AI data-centre and grid capex supports electrification names, but a falling Russell/Nasdaq ratio says cyclical breadth is lagging, and elevated aluminium premiums add input-cost pressure.

Reported: Dycom posted an earnings beat tied to AI infrastructure demand (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 27]), but its shares sank 10% (Investing.com, [Aug 26]). Qantas's profits dipped to a four-year low (The Guardian, [Aug 26]), yet its shares jumped as it unveiled new business-class seats (CNBC, [Aug 27]). Deere rallied 7% after quarterly profit climbed and it raised its full-year forecast (TIKR.com, [Aug 21]).

EPS Upside Watch: IES — sees a data-centre boom and plans a $650M DBM Global acquisition (TradingView, [Aug 27]). Delta — CEO Ed Bastian says AI could boost profits by 50% as the airline tests AI-set fares on 3% of tickets (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 24]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: This earnings season confirmed the AI power bottleneck is real (The Motley Fool, [Aug 27]), yet Dycom sank 10% on an AI-tied beat. The market already owns the build-out story, so industrials now need a raised guide, not AI exposure, to move.
Narrative: Amazon jumped on the week and Walmart adding Apple Pay shows digital payments still expanding, while discretionary results reward brands with pricing power and growth investment.

Reported: Best Buy beat quarterly estimates and hiked its outlook, but the stock fell (CNBC, [Aug 27]). Ulta lifted its annual forecasts as marketing and product investments fuel growth (Reuters, [Aug 27]). Abercrombie & Fitch posted record sales and raised guidance (Drapers, [Aug 27]).
EPS Upside Watch: Delivery Hero — lifted guidance on increased growth (WSJ, [Aug 27]). Halfords — raised its profit guidance after a boost from heatwaves (The Times, [Aug 27]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Positioning is beating prints: Best Buy's stronger forecast failed to reassure investors (Reuters, [Aug 27]), while Gap jumped 12% after naming a new Old Navy CEO (CNBC, [Aug 27]). A priced-in beat-and-raise sells, and a credible turnaround story pays, which makes the bullish call a stock-picker's market.
Narrative: Rising rates and risk-on positioning disfavour staples as a relative trade, and the latest prints show price carrying growth while volumes stall.

Reported: Hormel cut its annual sales forecast as sluggish consumer demand weighed (Reuters, [Aug 27]) and was the day's worst S&P 500 stock (Barron's, [Aug 27]). Dollar General's stock rose as it hiked earnings guidance (Barron's, [Aug 27]). Dollar Tree scored with tariff refunds, yet its stock fell (Barron's, [Aug 27]).
EPS Upside Watch: BJ's Wholesale — beat and raised its full-year EPS guidance (Quartz, [Aug 21]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Trade-down is reaching the dollar stores from the top: Dollar Tree is attracting higher-income customers as sales climb 7% (PYMNTS.com, [Aug 27]), but says tariff reinvestments will squeeze near-term profit (WSJ, [Aug 27]). Refunds are going back into price, not into earnings.
Narrative: Danaher is flagged as a compounder to watch and Edwards Lifesciences as the TAVR boom leader, and the sector benefits from defensive positioning if a hawkish Warsh lifts equity volatility.

Reported: Agilent beat estimates and raised guidance on strong demand, and its shares rose (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 26]). Veeva had its best day ever as the software sector rallied (Barron's, [Aug 27]). Ambu cut its full-year guidance (The Copenhagen Post, [Aug 26]).

EPS Upside Watch: Dexcom and Abbott — await a Medicare coverage expansion for CGMs (MedTech Dive, [Aug 27]), a volume lever for both. Pharmaron — raised its full-year revenue guidance, and Goldman Sachs and Daiwa lifted their target prices (BigGo Finance, [Aug 24]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Pharma reshoring is turning into orders for the tools makers: Agilent raised its outlook as core growth hit 7.3%, China rebounded 9% and pharma reshoring orders began (BigGo Finance, [Aug 26]). Factory building is an earnings tailwind for life-science tools that the defensive label hides.

Narrative: Copper at $6.66 (+3.5%), an AI data-centre and grid-capex metal, and elevated aluminium premiums support the complex, while gold at $4529 (+11.9%) is the standout that flows mostly to miners.

Reported: Harmony Gold's dividend soared as earnings jumped 87% (MiningMX, [Aug 27]). Hochschild Mining's shares jumped as earnings soared on higher gold and silver prices (WSJ, [Aug 26]). South32's annual profit jumped 55% and it extended its shareholder-returns program (Mining.com, [Aug 26]).

EPS Upside Watch: Sibanye-Stillwater — flags higher earnings on solid operations, higher prices and margins (Mining Weekly, [Aug 27]). Quaker Chemical — earnings estimates are moving higher (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 27]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Miners are paying out rather than spending: bumper payouts with more to come (AFR, [Aug 27]) and Harmony's soaring dividend send the gold windfall straight to shareholders, a discipline that can keep miners outperforming the metal itself.

Narrative: A hawkish Warsh and the risk of higher short-end rates (2Y at 4.20% prior close) are headwinds for rate-sensitive real estate, and Yahoo Finance asking whether the housing market will crash in 2026 captures the mood.

Reported: Waypoint REIT posted distributable earnings growth and confirmed its FY26 outlook (The Motley Fool Australia, [Aug 27]). Emirates REIT's 1H earnings fell 71%, but rental growth boosted underlying performance (EnterpriseAM, [Aug 27]).
